The two planets built for effortless charm and authority are the weakest things in his chart. He trained for the rest.

5 NOV 1988 · NEW DELHI

TL;DR

Two "easy" planets. Zero easy years.

In Vedic astrology, the Sun runs authority and the Venus runs charm — the two planets that are supposed to make a life feel effortless. In Virat Kohli's kundli, both are debilitated, the only two placements in the whole chart that are actually weak.
Nothing else in the chart is on home ground either — every other graha here is a neutral guest, not a native. There is no planet in this birth chart handing him anything for free.

And here's the part that lines up with the public record: one mahadasha has run his entire senior career. Rahu, since November 2009. The Test debut, every captaincy call, the wedding, his daughter's birth, both retirements — all inside the same eighteen-year stretch.

The loss, and the innings after

Unbeaten the day after his father's funeral
  • On 18 December 2006, his father Prem Kohli died suddenly. Kohli, 18, left the Ranji Trophy ground to attend the cremation and was back at the crease the next morning, batting to save the follow-on.
  • His India ODI debut followed on 18 August 2008.
🔭 The funeral and the innings fall in Mars MD / Mercury AD (May 2006–May 2007). The Sun — the general significator used for one's father elsewhere on these pages — is debilitated in this chart. A resonant echo, not a cause.

🔭 Rahu/Rahu → Rahu/Saturn, 2011–2017. Rahu is expansion and hunger; Saturn is the planet that hands you the whole responsibility at once.

The comeback, then two exits from the top

765 runs Player of the Tournament, 2023 ODI World Cup
  • An Asia Cup century in September 2022 snapped the drought — still Rahu/Venus, the renewal sub-period finally paying out.
  • The 2023 ODI World Cup on home soil followed, 765 runs and Player of the Tournament, still Venus.
  • India won the T20 World Cup on 29 June 2024 and he retired from T20Is immediately after — Rahu/Sun, the sub-period of peak recognition, winning and stepping back in the same breath.
  • He retired from Test cricket in May 2025, right at the Rahu/Sun → Rahu/Moon boundary — Moon being the emotional-turning-point planet, closing the format he has called his most personal.
🔭 Now in Rahu/Moon, through October 2026, still an active ODI player — with Rahu/Mars next, right as the wider Rahu mahadasha itself closes out in November 2027.

The tea ☕

Everything you're actually here for

Three things people actually search for. What the chart says about the pattern — not the gossip.

📉 The captaincy exit and the 1021-day drought
What's public

Between January 2020 and September 2022 he went without an international century — an unusually long drought for a player of his record. He gave up white-ball captaincy in 2021 and Test captaincy in January 2022, both amid heavy public and media scrutiny.

What the chart hints

The drought's end and the captaincy exit both sit right at the seam between Rahu/Ketu (release) and Rahu/Venus (his other debilitated planet) opening.

Astrologers would read that as a genuinely hard sub-period to walk into — and also the one that, months later, produced the century that ended it. A pattern, not a prediction.

😤 The send-offs and the sledging
What's public

His on-field aggression — send-offs, verbal exchanges with opponents, animated wicket celebrations — has been a consistent, widely covered part of his public image since early in his career.

What the chart hints

A debilitated Sun is a weak spot for the planet of ego and self-assertion — one traditional reading is that it pushes a person to assert authority more loudly, not less, precisely because it doesn't come easily.

Loud on the outside, working hard underneath. That's the placement in one line.

💍 Married under a magnifying glass
What's public

It's public record that sections of fans and commentators blamed Anushka Sharma for dips in his on-field form over the years — a pattern both he and she have publicly pushed back on and called unfair.

What the chart hints

Venus runs charm, partnership and how the public receives a relationship — and Venus is his other debilitated planet.

A weak Venus is traditionally read as affection that swings hard and unfairly in both directions, aimed at whoever's closest to the spotlight. It doesn't excuse the trolling; it's just the same placement showing up again.

Being straight with you: nobody outside someone's life knows why things really happen. None of the above is a claim about what happened or why — it's a traditional reading of a publicly known birth chart, for entertainment. Facts are public record; the astrology is interpretation.

Actually learn this

Astrology, but make it make sense

Zero background needed. Read this once and you can decode the birth chart above yourself — no astrologer required.

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

A kundli, or janam kundli, is a photo of the sky from the exact spot and second someone was born. Where each planet was sitting, frozen.

Vedic astrology treats that snapshot as the raw material a person was handed — not their fate, their starting kit.

His: his birthday is 5 November 1988, in New Delhi. That sky had the Sun and Mercury in Libra, the Moon and Venus in Virgo, Mars in Pisces. Those placements do most of the talking on this page.
LESSON 02

Nine of them, or navagraha. Think of them as nine departments, each running one part of a life.

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, different room, different output.

  • Home ground (own sign) — the planet owns the place. Full strength, no permission needed.
  • Debilitated (weakest spot) — it's working with the handbrake on.
  • Everywhere else (neutral) — a guest. Functional, not special.
His scorecard is unusual: two planets debilitated (Sun, Venus), and every single other planet — Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu — sitting neutral. Zero planets on home ground. Most charts have at least one; his has none. That's not a weak chart, it's a chart with no free placements at all.
LESSON 04

Dashas — why timing is the whole game

This is the bit most people have never heard of, and it's the most useful.

Planets don't all act at once. They take turns running a life, for years at a stretch, in a fixed order the Moon's position sets at birth. Vedic astrology calls a planet's turn a dasha, and the full sequence for a lifetime is called the Vimshottari dasha.

His turns, computed:
Sun 1988–92 · Moon 1992–2002 · Mars 2002–09 · Rahu 2009–2027 · Jupiter 2027–43 · Saturn 2043–62 · Mercury 2062–79

Look at that fourth one. Rahu has been running his life since he was 21, and doesn't hand over until he's 39.
LESSON 05

Sub-periods — the chapters inside the mahadasha

An eighteen-year turn is too blunt to be useful on its own, so it splits into shorter stretches, each run by one of the other planets. That's the level where the year-to-year story actually lives.

Inside his Rahu mahadasha:
Rahu/Rahu (2009–12) → Test debut
Rahu/Jupiter (2012–14) → RCB captaincy
Rahu/Saturn (2014–17) → full India captaincy
Rahu/Mercury (2017–20) → marriage, Khel Ratna
Rahu/Ketu (2020–21) → daughter born
Rahu/Venus (2021–24) → captaincy exit, then the comeback
Rahu/Sun (2024–25) → T20 World Cup win, retires from T20Is
Rahu/Moon (2025–26, current) → Test retirement, active in ODIs
LESSON 06

The one boundary that could change all of the above

Dasha order isn't set by the date alone — it's set by exactly which sliver of a lunar nakshatra the Moon sat in at the moment of birth. Twenty-seven nakshatras carve up the sky, each ruled by one planet, and whichever one the Moon occupies decides which planet's mahadasha runs first.

His Moon sits in Uttara Phalguni, ruled by the Sun — which is why his ladder above starts with a Sun mahadasha. But the nakshatra just before it, Purva Phalguni, is ruled by Venus, and the two are separated by a boundary that falls at roughly 3:05am on 5 November 1988.

A birth before that minute would put the Moon in Purva Phalguni instead — and the entire sequence in Lesson 05 would start with Venus, not Sun, shifting every date after it. Nobody has published a source claiming a pre-dawn birth for him, and the one unrated time in circulation (10:28am, via AstroSage) sits well on the Sun side. So this page runs the Sun-first sequence as primary — and tells you exactly where the seam is, rather than pretending it doesn't exist.
LESSON 07

What we genuinely can't tell you

Here's where most celebrity astrology sites quietly cheat, and we won't.

A chart has two halves. Which sign each planet is in — that only needs the date, so everything above is solid. And the houses, which need the exact minute of birth, because the rising sign changes roughly every two hours.

Nobody has published a verified birth time for him. The 10:28am figure that circulates is explicitly unrated by the astrology database quoting it, with no source trail behind it.

So on this page you will not see us say "his career house" or "his 7th house of marriage" — that would be a guess dressed as a fact. Other sites will. Ask them which birth time they used.
LESSON 08

So — is Virat Kohli manglik?

One of the most-searched questions about him, and the honest answer is uncomfortable.

"Manglik" depends on which house Mars occupies — a small set of specific spots tied to marriage. Houses need the birth time. Without one, this genuinely cannot be answered.

What we can say: his Mars sits in Pisces, a neutral placement by sign. Whether that lands in a manglik house depends entirely on an hour nobody has confirmed. Any site giving you a confident yes or no for him has picked a birth time and isn't telling you which.

Quick answers

What people ask about his kundli

FAQ 01

What is Virat Kohli's birth time?

No verified birth time exists. A time of 10:28am circulates on astrology sites, sourced to AstroSage, but it's explicitly unrated there with no documented trail. This page publishes only what holds without a confirmed birth time — his zodiac signs, nakshatra and dasha eras — and never houses, lagna or a manglik verdict.

FAQ 02

What is Virat Kohli's zodiac sign and nakshatra?

By Vedic reckoning, his Moon sign — also called his rashi — is Virgo, and his Moon's nakshatra is Uttara Phalguni (pada 2), the placement that sets his dasha sequence. His Sun sign is Libra, though Vedic (sidereal) and Western (tropical) zodiacs use different calculation methods, so his Western sun sign is often quoted as Scorpio. The full birth chart is above; every position is computed, not copied.

FAQ 03

Is Virat Kohli manglik?

This can't be honestly answered without a verified birth time, because manglik status depends on which house Mars occupies, not just its sign. What's known: his Mars sits in Pisces, a neutral placement by sign alone. Any source giving you a definite yes or no has assumed a birth time it isn't disclosing.

FAQ 04

Do Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma's kundlis match?

We can't run a real guna Milan compatibility check without a confirmed, public birth chart for Anushka Sharma, and we don't publish scores built on a guess. What's on public record is a marriage since December 2017 and a daughter born in 2021 — outcomes a chart can describe in hindsight, not verdicts it can hand out in advance.
